description: Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data
summary:
CropWise is a web-based agricultural decision-support platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, under the challenge Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data.

The project aims to help farmers make more informed agricultural decisions by combining NASA satellite-derived climate data, weather forecasts, geographic information, and user-provided farm details.

Rather than simply displaying environmental information, CropWise aims to translate data into practical crop recommendations, farming strategies, risk warnings, and trackable actions.
details:
CropWise is a web application we developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 to help farmers make better decisions using NASA Earth science data. Our goal is to make complex climate and environmental information easier to understand and useful for everyday farming.

Users can select their farm location on an interactive map and enter details such as their current crops, soil pH, irrigation availability, and farming goals. CropWise uses historical temperature and rainfall data from NASA POWER to recommend suitable crops and compare different crop rotation strategies. We also integrated NOAA and Open-Meteo to provide weather forecasts and help identify potential environmental risks. Farmers can review suggested actions and track their progress through the Reports & History feature.

We built CropWise using React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and Leaflet. We also used USDA agricultural parcel data for our Iowa demonstration area and localStorage to save farm information without requiring an account.

What makes CropWise different is that it connects environmental data with practical farming decisions instead of simply displaying charts and weather statistics. We focused on keeping the platform simple, accessible, and transparent about where its information comes from.

One of our biggest challenges was combining different data sources while supporting farms in different locations. We also had to consider that farmers have different crops, resources, and priorities, so we designed the recommendations to adapt to their inputs.

We hope CropWise can help farmers better understand their land, prepare for changing weather conditions, and make more informed and sustainable farming decisions without needing expensive monitoring equipment.
